message: Root implementation review observation (not independent verdict): replay fence currently checks deployment-submission.json inside newly acquired data plus native GET==404. A fresh workflow dispatch can reacquire the original immutable PREPARE artifact, which predates apply's journal/consumed receipts. After prior PUT response loss, a temporarily missing/404 native deployment record is not proof no submission occurred; new job could refresh what-if then send a second PUT for the same intent. Please exercise this concrete cross-job case using a fresh workspace restored from the original prepare archive, prior UNKNOWN, native history unavailable/404, and new authenticated workflow run. Require zero second PUT, preserving original ID. If current code already enforces it, retain actual evidence. Otherwise add a bounded authenticated durable intent fence independent of mutable/acquired artifacts (e.g. prior trusted control workflow dispatch/history under same scope serialization), not an unsigned receipt or documentation-only 'do not rerun'. New approval doesn't erase original UNKNOWN; reconciliation is read-only. Keep native API scope, no actual cloud, and distinguish fail-closed inability to establish history from permission to retry. This is the approved replay/recovery requirement, not a new resource engine.
